author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Set up PS2 emulation on an external monitor
summary: Connect one documented display chain, verify negotiated mode, aspect, overscan, game mode, audio route, controller response, and power stability against the phone baseline.
heroAlt: PCSX2 Big Picture interface displayed as the full-screen reference for an Android external-monitor setup

sourceLabels.android-frame-pacing: Android display synchronization and frame-pacing concepts

blocks.text: Treat the cable, adapter, monitor, and audio as one chain
Validate an Android-to-display chain for resolution, refresh, aspect ratio, safe insets, audio route, input latency, and stable power before using it for PS2 play.
An adapter can produce a picture while silently limiting refresh, adding latency, drawing unstable power, or routing sound to an unexpected device.

items: Phone video-output support and adapter specification confirmed.
Monitor input exposes its resolution, refresh, aspect, and game mode.
Power and controller arrangement tested separately on the phone.
1. Capture the phone-only scene including all four image edges.
2. Connect the adapter and monitor before changing emulator resolution.
3. Read the negotiated display mode from Android or the monitor information panel.
4. Set correct aspect and disable overscan or decorative zoom.
5. Enable the monitor's low-latency game mode for one paired comparison.
6. Choose and verify the intended audio output route.
7. Test controller response, camera pan cadence, and simultaneous sound.
8. Reconnect the complete chain and run a sustained power-and-temperature pass.

blocks.text: Comparing the same scene on the phone separates emulator rendering from faults introduced by the cable, adapter, display mode, or television processing.
The monitor shows correct aspect and complete edges, motion remains stable, audio uses the intended output, and controls stay responsive through reconnect.

items: All image edges and PS2 aspect geometry remain visible.
The monitor reports a stable supported refresh and resolution.
Audio, input, and power survive a complete disconnect and reconnect.
Edges are missing: disable overscan or zoom on the monitor.
Picture works but audio moves unexpectedly: select and verify the route.
Controls feel late only externally: compare monitor game mode and phone screen.
USB devices reset when display connects: inspect hub and power budget.

blocks.text: Return to the verified phone-only session
Disconnect the display chain and restore the phone's original refresh, audio route, and orientation policy.
Desktop-style secondary display behavior varies by Android device
Some phones mirror, some extend, and some negotiate only limited modes; confirm actual output rather than assuming the connector guarantees a capability.
